Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of our procurement and security review we need a focused set of answers around Support / TAM coverage and incident communications. Please provide concise answers or point to attachments for the following items by end of week: 

1) TAM coverage: are TAMs included in our contract tier? If so, what is the SLA for TAM response times and dedicated hours (e.g., weekly office hours, quarterly reviews)?
2) Escalation path: provide the escalation matrix for Sev1/Sev2/Sev3 incidents (roles, contact windows, SLA for escalation).
3) Support hours & routing: standard support hours (timezone), after-hours support availability, and primary routing (email, portal, phone, PagerDuty).
4) Incident comms: sample announcement templates for P1/P2 incidents, typical cadence (initial, updates, resolution), and expected content (impact, workaround, ETA).
5) On-call & rotation: how is on-call managed? Do you provide named contacts for our account?
6) Maintenance & planned downtime: notification windows and blackout windows for production.
7) Reporting & post-incident review: how are incident reports delivered and what is the SLA to provide RCA?
8) Escalation to execs: when/how do we escalate to leadership (TAM -> CS Ops -> VP/GM)?

If you have a pre-filled response pack or template, please attach. We will likely attach your answers verbatim into our RFI.

Best,
Sara Nguyen
Director, Vendor Risk & Ops
ApexBank

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. We can turn this around for you. Attached is a draft packet that addresses each item at a summary level; we propose to follow up with a short call to walk through details and share named contacts.

Quick highlights: 
- TAMs: included for our Enterprise tier; weekly office hours + quarterly business reviews. Standard TAM response target is 4 business hours for high-priority consults, with faster routing for Sev incidents.
- Escalation: we have a 4-tier matrix (Support -> TAM -> CS Ops -> Platform Escalation / Eng on-call). Sev1 escalation target: 15 minutes to acknowledge, 60 minutes to engage appropriate engineering resources.
- Support hours: 24/7 for Sev1 via PagerDuty + portal; regional SLA default in US business hours 09:00-18:00 PT for non-urgent items.
- Incident comms: we include an initial incident notice (T-minus impact + mitigation steps), regular 30–60 minute updates for active Sev1, and a final resolution + RCA commitment (RCA within 5 business days or sooner for critical incidents).

Attachments included: Redwood_Support_RFI_Draft.pdf (pdf), incident-comm-template.docx (docx).

Next steps: Marissa will finalize SLA language and uptime targets, Karthik will confirm the named on-call escalation contacts for your region, and Dev will attach a sample on-call roster/export. Can we book 30 minutes on Thursday (Apr 16) at 11:00 AM PT to walk through?

Thanks — looking forward to tightening this up.

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks for the opportunity. Attached is a consolidated response pack (ApexBank_RFI_Support_Responses_v1.pdf) and a sample on-call roster export. Below are direct, RFI-ready answers you can paste into your template; the attached PDF has more context and contract notes.

1) TAM coverage: Enterprise includes a named TAM. Deliverables: weekly office hours (1 hour/week), quarterly business reviews, and monthly health checks. TAM consult response target: 4 business hours for general inquiries; urgent consults routed via Support/PagerDuty for 4-hour or faster engagement. (Commercial note: dedicated 24/7 TAM is available as an add-on.)

2) Escalation path: Support -> TAM -> CS Ops -> Platform Engineering (on-call) -> Escalation Manager (Director/VP). Sev1 (Critical outage): acknowledgement target 15 minutes; engineering engagement target 60 minutes; continuous updates every 30–60 minutes until mitigation. Exec-level notification if incident remains unresolved after 8 hours or upon customer request.

3) Support hours & routing: 24/7 coverage for Sev1 incidents via PagerDuty and support portal. Standard business-hours support (US): 09:00–18:00 PT for non-critical issues. Primary routing: support.redwood.ai portal (ticket), support@redwood.example.com, and an assigned PagerDuty integration for critical incidents. Phone escalation available for named contacts.

4) Incident communications: initial notice within 15 minutes of acknowledgement for Sev1 with impact summary; cadence: initial, then 30–60 minute updates for active Sev1, targeted resolution message, and final RCA. Attached: incident-comm-template.docx (initial, update, resolution templates).

5) On-call & rotation: on-call is managed via PagerDuty; we can provide named on-call contacts for your account on request. We maintain a rotating primary and secondary on-call with documented handover. (See attached on-call-rotation.csv sample.)

6) Maintenance & planned downtime: customers are notified at least 72 hours prior for planned maintenance that may impact production; emergency maintenance communications follow the incident cadence. We support blackout windows for scheduled financial close windows by mutual agreement.

7) Reporting & post-incident review: full incident report and RCA delivered within 5 business days for Sev1 incidents; expedited RCAs can be provided if contractually required. The RCA includes timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation, and permanent fix plan.

8) Escalation to execs: route requests to your TAM; TAM will escalate to CS Ops and arrange VP/GM involvement if needed. Exec escalation is triggered by either customer request or if a Sev1 remains unresolved beyond 8 hours.

Next steps: please let me know a good time for a 30-minute walkthrough (we suggested Thu Apr 16 earlier — apologies for the scheduling confusion; can you do Tue Apr 21 10:00 AM PT instead?). If Apex wants named on-call contacts included in the PDF we will provide them after we confirm NDA/PO references.

Attachments: ApexBank_RFI_Support_Responses_v1.pdf, on-call-rotation.csv, incident-comm-template.docx

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
